title.narrative: Safeguarding Health and Protection: Integrated GBV and SRH Services for Communities Affected by STS Trami

description.narrative: The objective of this project is to provide life-saving sexual and reproductive health and Gender Based Violence services for women, girls and other vulnerable groups affected by STS Trami. Through this initiative, UNFPA will: (1) ensure the availability of critical sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services; and (2) deliver multi-sectoral support to prevent and respond to gender-based violence (GBV) for women, girls, persons with disabilities, and other at-risk populations. The direct target beneficiaries are 4,600 women for SRH services and information and 9,500 women, girls, boys and men with GBV prevention, mitigation, services and information. Indirect beneficiaries include 50,000 women and girls, and 10,000 men and boys in the affected areas. This project aims to restore access to life-saving services and strengthen community resilience in the face of the disaster’s impacts.Sexual and Reproductive Health - For SRH, key activities will include re-establishing and supporting regular SRH coordination meetings at regional and municipal levels in collaboration with local authorities to ensure effective service delivery. The project will also provide life-saving reproductive health kits, such as modern methods of contraceptives, essential health facility equipment and supplies (e.g., delivery tables, stethoscopes) to support ongoing SRH services. Cash assistance will be provided to pregnant women in their third trimester to facilitate access to SRH services in the six affected municipalities. Additionally, community mobilizers will be deployed to raise awareness on SRH issues, including maternal health, family planning, and menstrual hygiene management.Protection and Response to Gender-based Violence - The project will support the re-establishment of GBV sub-cluster meetings at regional and municipal levels to coordinate response efforts and distribute dignity and menstrual hygiene kits to women and girls at risk of GBV. Psycho-social support services, including counseling and mental health support, will be provided through skilled social workers. Women-friendly spaces will be established to offer safe environments for women, particularly GBV survivors, referring them to critical services like counseling, medical care, and legal assistance. The project will also update protection referral pathways to ensure timely, survivor-centered care and engage communities to raise awareness about SRH services, GBV prevention, and response, while establishing feedback mechanisms to enhance accountability and service quality.
